- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.27) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast upward by 1–2% to avoid underestimating rebound.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >70), model often overshoots in the next 5–7 days; reduce forecast peak by 3–5% and smooth the decline.
- If sentiment is high (≥0.7) and price is trending up, model frequently overestimates near-term gains; cap forecast growth at 1.5–2% above recent mean.
- When sentiment swings from positive to negative, model lags in adjusting downward; add 1–2 days of lagged correction (e.g., if sentiment drops, reduce forecast 1–2 days later).
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon; if forecast is >10% above recent 10-day average, reduce by 5–8% unless sentiment supports continuation.
- If sentiment is neutral (0.3–0.6) and price is volatile, model tends to overfit short-term noise; use 3-day moving average to filter out erratic spikes.
